newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks down in late trade on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks down in late trade on profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan's stocks fell in late trade on Tuesday with investors, turning cautious as the index neared the 10,000-point level, taking profits off the session's earlier gains, brokers said.
With 45 minutes left at 0315 GMT, the benchmark index was down 88.69 points or 0.9 percent at 9,745.08, off an intraday high of 9,877.39.
Turnover was heavy at T$135.9 billion.
Financials, which had been the leading gainers in the past two sessions, were down 0.48 percent. Electronics also dropped 0.76 percent despite rising earlier.
"Heavy profit-taking eroded the early gains, and the overall market is expected to consolidate," said Chen Han-chung, manager of Yungli Securities.
"As the index comes close to 10,000 points, investors are becoming cautious and are taking profits more frequently," he said.
Brokers said they already noticed an increase in sell orders following the market's initial rise.
"This means the index might end soft," said Joe Chiou, analyst for Taiwan Securities Investment.
Brokers said large sell orders were seen especially on financial shares.
